author: anon-df5e95db
content:
Instead of replacing tbx_readrec as a C callback, redesign tabix iteration to bypass hts_itr_query entirely. Use the bgzf crate for decompression and implement record parsing + index-based seeking in pure Rust. This would eliminate the tbx_readrec callback, hts_itr_query, hts_itr_next, and hts_get_bgzfp FFI calls in one sweep.

Approach:
1. Parse the .tbi index file directly (it's a standard binning index format)
2. Use the bgzf crate to seek to the right virtual offset and read BGZF blocks
3. Parse tab-separated records in Rust (trivial string splitting)
4. Implement region overlap filtering in Rust

This is a larger architectural change than the incremental leaf replacements — it replaces the entire tabix read pipeline. Low priority since the current FFI approach works and this is mostly about code ownership.

Dependencies: none (bgzf crate handles compression). Would obsolete #14 (tabix leaves) and #16 (hts_itr_query).
